subject: Reserved Capacity: GPU cost-sharing term proposal and fallback mechanics
messages:
From: Catherine Taylor <ctaylor@labsurge.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — need flexibility for GPU market swings

Hi Evelyn / David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look great. We are preparing an internal finance request for a 24-month reserved capacity commitment but procurement flagged GPU spot-price volatility as a material risk.

Two asks from our side before we escalate to legal:
1) Can Redwood include a limited-price-pass-through or indexation clause that adjusts the effective committed price if market GPU rates move >15% for a sustained 60-day window?
2) If there is an acute spike, can we trigger a temporary throttled-burst (lower committed baseline, with burst capacity billed at market adjustment) rather than fully re-negotiating?

We are sensitive to long tenors but like the idea of predictable committed baseline. I copied procure@labsurge.com — they may follow up with the standard contracting checklist.

Appreciate any flexibility you can offer; our procurement rhythm next week will determine whether we move forward this quarter.

Best,
Catherine Taylor
Head of Infrastructure
Labsurge

--

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — need flexibility for GPU market swings

Hi Catherine — thanks for the clear framing. Short answers up front: yes, we can propose a limited index clause and a burst/baseline fallback; we typically route the final wording through finance and legal but can outline the commercial construct now so you can present it internally.

What we propose as a starting point (attached spreadsheets summarize numerics):
- Baseline commitment: committed GPU units (vGPU-hours equivalent) at fixed unit price for 12 or 24 months (you pick tenor).
- Market adjustment corridor: if wholesale GPU market index (we recommend using the Redwood GPU Index) moves >+/-15% for 60 consecutive days, price for new tokens is adjusted by the percentage movement capped at +/-25% for that quarter.
- Acute spike fallback: customer can elect a "banded baseline" option — reduce committed baseline capacity by up to 30% for a single 90-day window once per 12 months; during the window, overflow/burst is available at an index-adjusted market rate (with a soft cap).
- One-time credit: for 24-month agreements we can offer a one-time onboarding credit applied to month 2 to offset partial coverage risk.

We are including two attachment stubs: a term-option matrix and worked examples for a 12 vs 24 month path. Kimberly is cc'd for pricing mechanics; David is on ops for activation phasing. If this construct looks acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute call Wed 09/08 or Thu 09/09 to agree on a mutual action plan and get procurement/legal language started?

Warmly,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding Labsurge's ask and Evelyn's proposed constructs. Quick notes for pricing/finance:
- Labsurge is evaluating a 24-month committed baseline but procurement wants protection for price shocks.
- Evelyn suggested a +/-15% trigger with a 60-day sustained window and a cap at +/-25% per quarter. That construct preserves some predictability but exposes us to downside if GPU costs spike >25%.
- They also want a one-time onboarding credit for 24-month deals.

Question: what is acceptable from a finance perspective to protect Redwood on tail risk? Options we should consider: a) pass-through up to 25% (no cap beyond), b) cap at 25% with a shared-cost corridor (Redwood absorbs X%, customer absorbs Y%), c) index + hedging language requiring joint quarterly review + optional reprice at renewal.

Can you sketch the preferred language and whether you need an expected-case/case-with-spike P&L to sign off? I can pull estimated GPU-weighted cost curves for the worked examples Evelyn attached.

-David

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — need flexibility for GPU market swings

Hi Catherine — sorry for the slight delay. I reviewed the proposed constructs with finance. High level decision and an approval path:

1) Approved commercial framework (pilotable):
   - Offer the 24-month commitment with the Market Adjustment Corridor as Evelyn outlined, but with a shared-risk split on movements beyond the 15% trigger. Specifically: Redwood absorbs the first 10% of any increase beyond the 15% trigger; customer absorbs the next 10%; beyond a 25% total movement, the parties enter a mandatory review and a one-time tranche reprice (not automatic pass-through). This limits Redwood's tail exposure while giving Labsurge predictable protections.

2) Acute spike fallback: approved up to 30% baseline reduction once per 12 months; burst capacity billed at index-adjusted rate with a quarterly soft cap.

3) Credits and offsets: for a signed 24-month agreement we will provide a one-time implementation credit equal to 2 months of committed baseline value (applied in month 2).

Next steps I propose for speed:
- Evelyn to send a short mutual action plan (MAP) with dates for procurement/legal review and target sign date.
- Labsurge to confirm whether they prefer a 12- or 24-month tenor; if 24-month, we will provision the credit and the shared-risk corridor above.
- We will prepare contract language and circulate via DocuSign link (placeholder below) for procurement review by 09/15.

If that sounds workable, Evelyn — can you lock in Wed 09/10 10:00am PT for a final pricing alignment call? Catherine — if that time works for you, please mark it and I will send calendar invites.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
